items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer mentions Milt Jackson in the context of recording credits for 'Opus de Funk', but the interviewee (Maxine Sullivan) does not mention any personal interaction, collaboration, or relationship with Milt Jackson.

ctx.x: He was a very well-known radio announcer and disc jockey at the time. The -- right after the theme, the band goes into a little up-tempo selection which is not identified on the album. But it was one of Kirby's original selections. I think you mentioned that someone else had recorded it, and it was called "Opus de Funk," or something like that.
That's right. I remember it's a side of Milt Jackson or Horace Silver composition recorded, I think, in the late 40's under the title "Opus de Funk," on the Savoy label if I'm not mistaken.
Well, if it's the one I'm thinking about (humming tune) --
